title: Colored fills can make day numbers, selected icons and Undo text hard to read
scope: Backlog only. Rendered contrast observations; no corrective app changes authorized by UX-001. Preserve the user's deliberate vivid Theme shade shift.
environment: Qt 6.12.0 MSVC 2022 x64, native Windows D3D11 WARP, production Weekdays/IconButton/UndoBar in an isolated review harness. Not reproduced as a physical-phone shopping incident.
evidence: With default Indigo/Green in Dark, the current-day number on its primary circle is 2.31:1; the selected theme icon and full-fill Undo text on accent are 1.43:1. Default Light selected-icon contrast is 1.67:1.

Across the 19 color families, current-day numbers are below 4.5:1 for 15 Light/19 Dark cases; selected icons below 3:1 for 10 Light/13 Dark cases; full-fill Undo text below 4.5:1 for 4 Light/18 Dark cases.

Default Green Undo was sampled over all ten backgrounds at full/half/empty progress in both themes. Dark full-fill text is 1.43:1, while empty-area samples are 5.77-9.08:1. The two surfaces need coordinated treatment.
Native screenshots and retained palette/underlay measurements are linked in reviews/UX-001.md.
reproduction: Run the explicit review probe documented in reviews/UX-001.md against the current Windows test executable.
Use Dark theme with Indigo primary and Green accent; inspect the Weekdays current-day circle, highlighted IconButton and full Undo progress fill.
Compare the foreground colors to actual filled backgrounds; repeat with Light theme and Green accent, and with Yellow/Lime or neutral choices.
Before implementing, add permanent regression assertions on these production components, prove they fail, and confirm the real Android UI paths (theme selection, Undo, and the pulled day header).
expected: Text and essential icons remain distinguishable on primary/accent fills across supported palette choices and themes. Keep vivid colors where practical; pair foreground and fill deliberately rather than assuming white or the normal theme foreground always works.
implementation_notes: Do not simply revert the Theme shade shift: the lighter Dark primary improves current-day name readability, and stock Qt highlighted Green also has low white-on-fill contrast.
The current-day name and number-circle need separate foreground/container roles even when they share a primary family.
An appropriate dark/light icon foreground can retain a bright selected-button fill.

UI-024 intentionally makes Undo text/icon follow normal TextItem colors. Any exception needs explicit design acceptance; a compatible same-family fill tone can preserve that policy. Account for the moving fill and uncovered translucent area together.
Prefer a small local rule or helper over a broad theme/framework rewrite. UX-001 is analysis, not authorization to apply its suggestions.
acceptance_criteria: Record a failing-before/passing-after automated rendered regression for the actual foreground/fill pairings; a measurement-only probe passing is not regression proof.
Use appropriate targets: 4.5:1 for small text, 3:1 for qualifying large text and meaningful icons; document any typography-based classification.
Cover representative bright, dark and neutral palettes, Light/Dark/System, and Undo full/partial/empty fills over actual backgrounds.
Preserve the intended shade shift, one-handed actions, opacity, inverse checked state and accepted Undo timing/interaction; document any intentional departure from UI-024 foreground policy.
Verify the relevant native Android paths with isolated data and record exact platform coverage before closure.
